text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Guntis Ulmanis and Foreign Minister Valdis Birkvas are to head to Madrid for the NATO summit where a decision on expanding the alliance will be taken. Birkavs is to send a letter to NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, setting out the hope for a clear prospect for Baltic NATO entry.
- Latvia's Kristers Sergis and Artis Rasmanis took second place in the sixth leg of the world motocross with sidecar championship. The event took place in a town some 50 km from Riga.
- The parliamentary faction For Fatherland and Freedom/LNNK met with candidates to the post of state minister of health. The faction plans to make decision on the post on July 10.
- The former faction of the National Conservative Party and the Green Party decided to change its name.
- The secretary-general of of the Committee of the International Red Cross, George Weber, called on Latvia's parliament to adopt a law on the Red Cross during a visit.
- A new law on compulsory social insurance could be adopted at parliament's extraordinary session and come into force from January 1, 1998.
- Minister of Economics Guntars Krasts is taking part in a conference on the global information network in Bonn.
- The meeting of a working group on the social and humanitarian issues of a Latvian-Russian intergovernmental commission will take place in Riga this week.
- Assemblers and manufacturers of computer equipment in Latvia as well as a number of computer scientists have formed a Computer Technology Manufacturers Association.

- Transit traffic through Latvian ports increased in the first five months of 1997 by 2.5 million tons compared with the same period of previous year. The total cargo turnover through Latvian ports was 20.9 million tons in the first five months.
